context_before: // JADE-MODERNIZATION-DEFERRED:TRY_WITH_RESOURCES Extremely broad pattern (1832 flags), deferred for targeted future review

patterns.reason: terminally deprecated ThreadGroup member invoked on one of the workspace's own ThreadGroup-typed fields (FullResourceManager.java:39-42, Runtime.java:73). Revision 1 was the untyped '\.destroy\(\)' and caught two java.applet.Applet.destroy() calls; a line-based regex cannot resolve the receiver's type, so revision 2 enumerates the ThreadGroup-typed receivers actually declared in this tree. The limitation is deliberate and recorded: a ThreadGroup held in a differently named variable would not be flagged, which is why the verification hint checks with javac rather than with this regex

rule_description: JDK 16 terminally deprecated ThreadGroup.stop, destroy, isDestroyed, setDaemon and isDaemon, stating that the API and mechanism for destroying a ThreadGroup is inherently flawed and will be removed in a future release. jade.core.Runtime calls destroy() on its time-critical ThreadGroup during shutdown, inside a try/catch that already tolerates IllegalThreadStateException and a finally that nulls the field. On JDK 17 the call still works, so nothing is broken today; the fix is to drop the call and keep the field reset, which is what the JDK's own guidance amounts to. The pattern is receiver-enumerated rather than general: 'x.destroy()' cannot be resolved to ThreadGroup by a line-based scanner, and the untyped form scored 0.33 against the 0.7 gate.
verification_hint: Recompiling on jade-ant:17 with -Xlint:removal reports no '[removal] destroy() in ThreadGroup' warning. A JADE container still shuts down cleanly and all consumers PASS.
